Subject: Newspark + Redwood: Reranker integration — post-demo notes & questions

Hi Priya / Sam —

Thanks again for the demo call this morning — really appreciated the overview of your current ranking stack and the examples you shared. Quick recap + a consolidated set of follow-ups that will help us scope the two-week eval we discussed:

1) Integration surface (priority order)
   - SDK setup & auth: you mentioned a node-based backend and Python infra for batch jobs. We can provide both SDKs — need to confirm auth method (service-token vs mTLS).
   - Request routing: whether you prefer per-request routing to a reranker pool or centralized prefilter -> rerank flow.
   - Embeddings -> reranker flow: your offline index vs live embedding compute (we saw both patterns today).
   - Structured output / tool-calls: you have downstream actions that rely on structured scoring metadata (confidence, signal reasons). We support tool-calling and stable JSON outputs.

2) Evaluation goals / metrics
   - Baseline metrics to measure: MRR, NDCG@10, Recall@K (K=50/100) and relative latency at p50/p95.
   - Target improvements: 10–15% relative NDCG uplift was the initial goal you mentioned.

3) Tuning knobs we should exercise during the eval
   - ranking API: top_k prefilter, top_k rerank, soft vs hard score thresholds, feature usage in ranking model.
   - embeddings: dimensionality / quantization / index (IVF vs HNSW) that affect recall vs latency.

Action items I need from you to prepare the trial environment:
  - Confirm which auth mechanism you prefer (service token or mTLS).
  - Share a small sample of production-ish query -> gold answers (10–50 items) and an exported index snapshot or clear readme for how you produce the index.
  - Expected SLA for p95 latency (helps sizing).

I attached a short proposal and an SDK snippet pack. Monica will follow up with technical details for the SDK/auth pieces.

Proposed next steps:
  - We spin up a dedicated evaluation space for Newspark next week (no infra change on your side beyond giving us a test service token),
  - Exchange sample data and metric definitions by EOD Wed (2027-04-14),
  - 2-week evaluation window with weekly check-ins (Monica + Sam + Priya + Rishi)

Thanks — looking forward to your confirmations.

Best,
Rishi

Thanks Rishi — super helpful recap. A few clarifying questions before we hand to infra: 

1) Auth: we generally use short-lived service tokens today (rotated by our secrets manager). We could trial mTLS for the evaluation if you recommend it — what are the tradeoffs you see for quick setup?

2) Prefiltering: currently we run an ANN index (HNSW) to produce top_200 then a light model to filter down to top_30 before our reranker. Would you recommend letting Redwood handle the entire prefilter->rerank or just plugging the reranker into our prefiltered top_30?

3) Metrics: we can share a 50-query goldset — curious if Redwood has a recommended way to compute NDCG when you have multiple relevance levels (exact match, partial match, related).

4) Latency: our target p95 for rerank is <120ms. Does that include network hop to your hosted service, or do you report server-only p95?

If Monica can drop example call payloads and a suggested config for top_k values, we can route this to infra tomorrow.

—Priya

Hi Priya / Sam —

Great questions — answering inline and attaching a short SDK snippet pack. See attached sdk-snippet.txt with examples for Node + Python.

1) Auth tradeoffs
   - Service token (short-lived): fastest to onboard (you mint tokens via your secrets manager and we validate via our token service). Works well for trial environments.
   - mTLS: stronger mutual auth, useful if you want to avoid token circulation. Slightly more setup (certificate provisioning), not required for an initial eval. For your 2-week trial I recommend short-lived service tokens.

2) Prefiltering recommendations
   - Given you already produce top_200 via HNSW + light model -> top_30, the lowest-friction path is to call Redwood's reranker with your top_30 payloads (we accept a list of candidate doc ids + embeddings or raw text).
   - If you want us to own the ANN stage later, we can host an index and handle prefiltering; that adds engineering effort but can reduce end-to-end latency in some configs.

3) NDCG with multiple relevance levels
   - We support graded relevance NDCG. Map your labels to grades (exact=3, partial=2, related=1). We'll compute NDCG@k with those weights. We'll also report MRR and Recall@K.

4) Latency reporting
   - Our standard reports separate client-to-server network time and server processing time. The SLA covers server-side p95. For fairness in your constraint (<120ms p95), we recommend measuring end-to-end from your environment once tokens are in place.

5) top_k guidance (initial config)
   - Prefilter top_k: 200 (your current)
   - Rerank candidates: start with top_50 then trim to top_10 for downstream surfacing
   - For compute/latency tradeoff, try rerank_top_k=50, scoring_batch_size=8 for first run

Attached: sdk-snippet.txt (examples), sample-payloads.json (example request/response). I can also provision a temporary test token if you confirm service-token flow.

Let me know and I can open the eval space.

—Monica
